Course

The Queen and the hive: how the t27 project builds itself

This project builds itself: an issue becomes a task for a bee, the bee writes a t27 spec, a reviewer bee checks it, it merges, and the site regenerates. The Queen who runs that loop is written as t27 specs with tests, and every widget here runs the fn bodies of one of them compiled to WebAssembly.

Course 11, 27 lessons, a live widget and a t27 spec each: shaping an issue, priority and review first, a task's life, the reviewer and the merge gate, the review jam, keys, credit and tokens, agents in one group, the night watch and the board. Every answer comes from a compiled spec.

Open the interactive course → Whole course on one page →

Every course is free, for everyone: no sign-up, no email, nothing to pay.

All lessons

  • Module 1 · The task

    An issue becomes work only once it is shaped: the sections it lacks are written or asked for, its boundary names real files, and one filter reads every kind of task.

    1. 01 Shaping an issue
    2. 02 A boundary of real files
    3. 03 One task, three kinds

  • Module 2 · Who goes next

    The order the Queen takes issues in: a label ages one step, at most 3 criticals run as critical, and nothing new starts while finished work waits for review.

    1. 04 Aging a label
    2. 05 The queue
    3. 06 Review first

  • Module 3 · A bee's life

    From candidate to done: twelve states and sixteen events, a ship in the game that flies home, and a deploy that does not cut a bee short.

    1. 07 A task's life
    2. 08 The ship flies home
    3. 09 A deploy mid-flight

  • Module 4 · The reviewer bee

    Finished work is judged on its own clock: enough reviews at once to keep up, a pause that doubles for a row that waits, and a merge gate that zero checks cannot open.

    1. 10 Enough reviewers
    2. 11 Back off
    3. 12 The merge gate

  • Module 5 · The review jam

    A pull request that will not move is in exactly one of ten cases, each with the Queen's move, and a red check is inherited only when master says so.

    1. 13 The review jam
    2. 14 The Queen's move
    3. 15 Inherited red

  • Module 6 · Keys

    A bee's model key can be refused: the code in the body sorts the refusal, a transient one rests the key for seconds, and the bee moves on to the next free key.

    1. 16 A refused key
    2. 17 A key rests
    3. 18 The next key

  • Module 7 · Credit and money

    Lending a key earns no credit, an operation is sold at twice its cost in half-cent tokens, and tokens burn 30 days after they land.

    1. 19 No credit for keys
    2. 20 Twice the cost
    3. 21 Tokens that burn

  • Module 8 · Agents among themselves

    One bot per agent in one group: who is called, a chain three bot messages deep, and the clocks that keep agents from flooding a chat.

    1. 22 Who is called
    2. 23 Three bots deep
    3. 24 Stop and mute

  • Module 9 · Night and the board

    What the hive shows: a night watch that opens, comments on and closes issues, the columns of the public board, and the comb that flashes for each event.

    1. 25 The night watch
    2. 26 The public board
    3. 27 The comb answers

TRI CLAW

The agent behind t27, in Telegram and on GitHub

TRI CLAW is the project's agent: it writes and checks .t27 specs with you. Three ways to use it.

  • Free, with your own key

    Add your own API key (NVIDIA or z.ai today) and the agent runs on it. Add more keys any time.

    Add a key in Telegram ↗

  • We do it for you

    No keys to keep: join the club in our Telegram bot and the agent runs on ours. The bot shows the price before you pay.

    Join the club in Telegram ↗

  • On GitHub

    TRI CLAW is also a GitHub App, built to check the .t27 specs a pull request changes. It is not open to other repositories yet.

    Read about TRI CLAW ↗
